# Didache Chapter 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_012_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 12

**1** Let every one who comes in the name of the Lord be received; then, testing him, you will know him — for you will have understanding to the right hand and to the left.

**2** If the one coming is a traveler, help him as much as you are able; but he shall not remain with you except for two or three days, if there is need.

**3** But if he wishes to settle down among you, being a craftsman, let him work and eat.

**4** But if he has no trade, according to your understanding, see to it that no Christian lives among you in idleness.

**5** But if he does not wish to act in this way, he is trafficking in Christ. Beware of such people.

---

*EMET notes: V.1 — "understanding to the right hand and to the left" = you will have discernment in both directions — a biblical idiom for complete wisdom (cf. Deut 5:32; 2 Kgs 22:2). V.3 — "craftsman" (τεχνίτης) = a skilled worker. The community is not to support able-bodied workers who refuse to work — cf. 2 Thess 3:10, "If anyone is not willing to work, let him not eat." V.5 — "trafficking in Christ" (χριστέμπορος) is a remarkable compound Greek word, unique to the Didache: literally "Christ-merchant/trader" — using Christ's name as a commercial vehicle. This is one of the strongest condemnations in the text.*
